parole.significato: A Turkish cold drink made from yoghurt and water with salt and sometimes herbs.
parole.testo: From a Turkic source, probably from Ottoman Turkish آیران (hence Turkish ayran).
From Turkic elements meaning “White Sheep”; compare Turkish ak and koyun.

parole.significato: A kind of cotton cloth from India.
parole.testo: Ultimately of Turkic origin: compare Ottoman Turkish آلاجه (alaca), Azerbaijani alaca (“multi-colored”). Also from Turkic: Persian الاچه (alâča), Russian алача́ (alačá), аладжа́ (aladžá).

parole.significato: The people living in the region of the Altai mountains.
parole.testo: From the Turkic word for "Golden Mountain". Compare Turkish altın (“gold”), dağ (“mountain”) and al (“red, colorful”) which altın is likely related to.

parole.significato: A village elder in some Central Asian cultures.
parole.testo: From various Turkic languages, including Bashkir аҡһаҡал (aqhaqal), Kazakh ақсақал (aqsaqal) and Kyrgyz аксакал (aksakal).

parole.significato: A long tight-waist jacket worn by the peoples of the Caucasus and Iran, made of various kinds of fabric, such as silk,…
parole.testo: From Turkic: compare Azerbaijani arxalıq, Turkish arkalık.

parole.significato: A Muslim people originally from north-west China who currently reside in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, and Russia.
parole.testo: From Turkic [Term?], probably via Russian, originally referring to any Hui Chinese. It is an exonym. Chinese scholar Lin Tao compiles a list of possible etymologies in Donggan yü lungao (2007): * From Chinese 東甘 /东甘 (dōng Gān, literally “Eastern Gan[su]”) — by a Russian consul in Ghulja of the name

parole.significato: A skilled horseman in the Caucasus and Central Asia.
parole.testo: From Turkic languages (compare Nogai йигит (yigit), Tatar егет (yeget, “young male”)), via Russian джиги́т (džigít).

parole.significato: A hot dusty northeasterly wind in the Tarim Basin in Central Asia.
parole.testo: From a term in some Turkic language roughly meaning "black wind": see Proto-Turkic *kara (“black”), *bora(n) (“north wind”).

parole.significato: A rural settlement (originally for the winter period) of seminomadic Turkic peoples of Central Asia, Azerbaijan and Afg…
parole.testo: Borrowed from a Turkic source. Cognates include Turkish kışlık, (colloquial) kışlak, kışla (“barracks”), Azerbaijani qışlaq, Uyghur قىشلاق (qishlaq), Karakhanid قِشْلاغْ (qıšlaɣ), Old Turkic 𐰴𐰃𐰽𐰞𐰍 (k¹is¹l¹g¹) and Yakut кыстык (kïstïk).

parole.significato: A member of a (possibly Turkic) people or tribe who lived around the Caspian before the arrival of the Avars.
parole.testo: Possibly a native Turkic formation; see Sabir. Cognate to Greek Σαβίνος (Savínos), Σάβιροι (Sáviroi).

parole.significato: A Central Asian bun stuffed with meat and sometimes with vegetables.
parole.testo: From Central Asian Turkic, from Classical Persian سَنْبوسَه (sanbōsa), from Middle Persian *sambōsag. Doublet of samosa and sambuseh.

parole.significato: A subarctic zone of evergreen coniferous forests situated south of the tundras and north of the steppes in the Northern…
parole.testo: From Russian тайга́ (tajgá), from South Siberian Turkic (Altai region, for example the Altay or Shor language, cf Khakas: тағ (tağ)), or alternatively Yakut тайга (tayga, “untraversable forest”). Doublet of Tayga.

parole.significato: A member of any Tungusic people.
parole.testo: From Russian тунгус (tungus), * supposedly deriving from donki, a self-designation of certain Siberian groups, or alternatively from a Yakut name for the Evenki. * Or, of East Turkic origin, from tunguz (“wild boar, pig”), from Old Turkic [script needed] (tonguz), from Proto-Turkic *toŋuz. * A contr
